key_insight: SVC treats each singular-vector channel as a controllable unit of plasticity, selectively updating only the channels that best balance new-task learning and preservation of pretrained knowledge.
engineering_relevance: This provides a principled, parameter-efficient way to adapt LLMs to new domains while reducing catastrophic forgetting, which is important for reliable continual deployment.
method: Estimate each channel’s adaptation benefit from domain-specific fine-tuning data.
Estimate forgetting cost using a fixed public general-domain corpus as a history-activation proxy.
Select trainable channels with knee-based cost screening, Pareto-front filtering, and Otsu thresholding.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports results across four LLM families and eight downstream tasks, with stronger pretrained-capability retention and competitive downstream performance versus PEFT baselines.
watch_item: Channel scoring depends on proxy estimates and thresholding heuristics, so performance may be sensitive to corpus choice and selection settings.
paper_title: Stability-Plasticity Balance via Singular-Vector Selection in LLM Continual Learning
